FYP Title: Cross-Platform Mobile Penetration Testing Framework for Android and iOS (TestFlight)
FYP Description:
This Final Year Project aims to design and implement a penetration testing framework for evaluating the security of mobile applications on both Android and iOS platforms. Android applications will be tested using APK-based security assessment techniques, while iOS applications distributed through TestFlight will be analyzed using dynamic security testing methods.

The framework will identify common mobile security vulnerabilities such as insecure data storage, weak authentication, insecure API communication, improper session management, SSL/TLS misconfigurations, and authorization flaws. The project will utilize industry-standard tools such as Burp Suite, MobSF, Frida, Objection, OWASP Mobile Security Testing Guide (MSTG), and OWASP Mobile Top 10 to perform comprehensive security assessments.

The outcome will be a standardized methodology and reporting system that enables developers to identify, reproduce, and remediate security vulnerabilities before releasing applications to production

FYP Title: Cross-Platform Live Game Streaming and Esports Community Platform
FYP Description:
This Final Year Project aims to develop a cross-platform mobile application for Android and iOS that enables gamers to live stream their gameplay, interact with viewers, and build gaming communities. Users can broadcast live game sessions, participate in real-time chat, follow their favorite streamers, receive notifications when creators go live, and watch recorded highlights. The platform will also support esports tournaments, team creation, leaderboards, and player profiles.

To enhance the user experience, AI features such as automatic highlight detection, stream summarization, toxicity detection in chat, and personalized game or streamer recommendations will be integrated. The application will provide a complete ecosystem for gamers, content creators, and esports enthusiasts while ensuring low-latency live streaming and scalable cloud infrastructure.

FYP Title: Gamified Speech Therapy Platform Using Fine-Tuned Automatic Speech Recognition
FYP Description: t: This one-year project aims to develop a comprehensive digital intervention platform for children with Speech Sound Disorders (SSDs). The system consists of an interactive, voice-controlled mobile application for patients and a data analytics dashboard for Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs). At its core, the project utilizes deep learning acoustic models (like Wav2Vec 2.0) to calculate Goodness of Pronunciation (GOP) scores at the phoneme level, rather than just transcribing text. By integrating AI-driven phonetic analysis with adaptive game mechanics, the platform ensures consistent, high-quality home practice while giving therapists remote data to optimize treatment plans
Tools/Technologies: App & Web: Flutter (Mobile) and React.js (Web Dashboard).Backend & Database: Python (FastAPI) and MongoDB.AI & Audio Processing: Python, PyTorch, and Wav2Vec 2.0 (for speech analysis).Cloud Storage: Firebase (to securely store audio logs).

FYP Title: Tajweed-AI – Automated Quranic Pronunciation Coach
FYP Description: Tajweed-AI is an interactive application that helps users learn and perfect their Quranic recitation using artificial intelligence. Instead of just checking if a user says the right word, the app's custom AI listens to specific phonetic rules (like Makharij/articulation points and Sifat/characteristics of letters). It gives real-time feedback on elongation (Madd), nasalization (Ghunnah), and correct letter placement. It also features a teacher dashboard to assign specific Surahs and track students' progress
Tools/Technologies: Flutter (Mobile) and Python/FastAPI (Backend), the app uses fine-tuned Wav2Vec 2.0 AI models

FYP Title: VidiWear: AI-Powered Video-to-Commerce Platform for Automated Fashion Recognition
FYP Description: VidiWear is a mobile and web ecosystem that turns any video clip (like a TikTok, Reel, or movie scene) into an instant digital storefront. When a user uploads a video, the system automatically detects, tags, and tracks multiple fashion items worn across frames in real-time. By translating visual apparel attributes into mathematical data, the app immediately matches clothes from the video to active online retail stores, offering users options for exact luxury matches or affordable, budget-friendly duplicates ("dupes") with clickable purchase links.

FYP Title: SpineAlign AR: An Edge-AI Computer Vision System with Real-Time Biomechanical Analytics for Lumbar Disc Herniation Rehabilitation.
FYP Description: SpineAlign AR is an innovative digital therapeutics platform designed specifically for patients recovering from a lower-back disc bulge or herniation. Using a standard smartphone camera, the application captures real-time 3D skeletal data to monitor the user's posture during rehabilitation exercises. The system uses advanced mathematical algorithms to track precise lumbar flexion angles, spine shear-stress, and hip compensations. If the patient performs a movement that compresses the spinal discs (such as dangerous forward bending or twisting), the app immediately triggers predictive 3D spatial audio warnings and visual heatmaps to prevent reinjury at home.

FYP Title: Synthetic Advanced Persistent Threats
FYP Description: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are among the most sophisticated cyberattacks, but obtaining real-world APT datasets for research and experimentation is challenging due to their sensitive nature and limited availability. This project aims to design and develop a framework for generating synthetic APT attack scenarios that closely emulate the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) of real adversaries. The generated attack campaigns will be used to create realistic datasets for evaluating intrusion detection systems, threat-hunting techniques, and AI-based cybersecurity solutions. The project will provide a safe and controlled environment for cybersecurity research, enabling the testing and validation of defense mechanisms without exposing production systems to actual cyber threats.

FYP Title: Trust Evaluation Framework for Shared CTI
FYP Description: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) sharing enables organizations to collaboratively defend against emerging cyber threats. However, the effectiveness of shared CTI is often affected by the lack of trust in intelligence sources and the varying quality of the shared information. Inaccurate, outdated, incomplete, or irrelevant threat intelligence can lead to poor security decisions and delayed incident response. This project aims to design and develop a framework that enhances the trust and quality of shared CTI. The proposed framework will assign trust and quality scores to CTI, enabling Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to prioritize reliable and high-quality intelligence. The project will support more effective threat intelligence sharing, improve cybersecurity decision-making, and strengthen collaborative cyber defense.

FYP Title: Digital Will
FYP Description: As people increasingly store personal, financial, and professional information online, managing digital assets after death has become a growing challenge. This project aims to design and develop a Digital Will Management System that allows users to securely record their wishes regarding digital assets such as email accounts, cloud storage, social media accounts, digital documents, and cryptocurrency wallets. The system will ensure that only authorized individuals can access or manage these assets based on the user's predefined instructions. By incorporating modern security mechanisms such as encryption, authentication, and access control, the proposed solution will protect users' privacy while enabling the secure and reliable transfer or management of digital assets. The project will contribute to addressing the emerging challenges of digital inheritance and digital estate planning in today's connected world.

FYP Title: AI-Assisted Detection of Secret Leakage in Android Applications
FYP Description: Develop an intelligent framework that combines static code analysis with large language models (LLMs) to identify hardcoded API keys, cloud credentials, authentication tokens, and cryptographic secrets in Android applications. The framework would prioritize high-risk leaks using contextual analysis and suggest automated remediation. This research improves software supply-chain security while reducing false positives compared to traditional static analyzers.

FYP Title: Adversarially Robust Android Malware Detection
FYP Description: Design a malware detection system resilient to code obfuscation, adversarial attacks, and polymorphic malware. The project would integrate static features, behavioral analysis, and graph neural networks to detect evolving malware families. Explainable AI techniques would help security analysts understand why an application is classified as malicious, improving trust and deployment in real-world environments.

FYP Title: Privacy-Preserving Permission and Data Flow Analysis for Android
FYP Description: Investigate how Android applications misuse permissions and sensitive user data despite complying with platform policies. The project would build an automated framework to trace information flow from sensitive sources (location, contacts, microphone, camera) to external destinations. Machine learning could distinguish legitimate data sharing from privacy violations, helping users and developers make informed security decisions.

FYP Title: Secure Sensor Authentication for Android Devices
FYP Description:
Design a hardware-backed authentication mechanism that verifies the authenticity of sensor data (fingerprint, camera, accelerometer, gyroscope, NFC) before applications consume it. This would protect against sensor spoofing and malicious data injection attacks.
Current Android applications generally trust whatever data the operating system provides. If the OS is compromised (e.g., by rooting, kernel exploits, or sophisticated malware), applications cannot easily determine whether sensor data has been manipulated.

Your proposed framework introduces a two-layer trust model:

1. Hardware-backed attestation confirms the data originated from trusted hardware.
2. AI-based behavioral analysis verifies that the sensor readings are physically plausible and consistent across multiple sensors.

FYP Title: AI-Based Smart Forest Protection and Illegal Tree Cutting Alert System
FYP Description:

Solution:

* GPS location of detected event
* SMS/mobile notifications to forest officials
* Android monitoring application
* Dashboard showing forest activity

Tools

* Microphone sensor
* GPS module
* TensorFlow Lite
* Firebase
* Android Studio
* Python

Machine Learning
CNN or LSTM for environmental sound classification.
